definition: CanJS is a JavaScript framework and toolkit for building reactive web user interfaces with observable data and templating.
example: An application updates a customer list when records change without manually redrawing the entire page.

definition: Cannabis and hemp extraction is the regulated processing of plant material to separate its chemical constituents from the plant matrix.
example: A quality reviewer checks the analytical results and traceability records for an extract batch.

definition: Cannabis cultivation is the production and care of cannabis plants under established growing and applicable regulatory requirements.
example: A compliance reviewer examines records showing how a permitted crop was tracked.

definition: Canon EOS flash systems are compatible camera and flash components for controlling artificial light during exposure.
example: A photographer uses a compatible flash to balance a subject’s illumination against a bright background.

definition: Canva is a visual design platform for creating graphics, presentations, and related media with editable layouts and templates.
example: A community group adapts a shared event flyer for print and social media.

definition: Canvas LMS is a learning management system for organizing courses, assignments, assessment, and communication.
example: An instructor publishes a module and collects assignments through Canvas.

definition: CanvasJS is a JavaScript charting library for rendering interactive data visualizations in web applications.
example: A developer builds an online chart that lets users examine a specific week’s readings.

definition: Capacity management aligns available resources with current and anticipated demand to maintain service performance.
example: A technology team estimates when storage demand will outgrow available capacity.

definition: Capistrano automates remote execution and deployment tasks for software applications.
example: A team runs a consistent release sequence across several authorized application servers.

definition: Capture One is photography software for processing raw files, organizing images, and tethered capture.
example: A studio checks exposure and focus as images arrive from a connected camera.

definition: Capybara is a Ruby web-testing library that simulates user interactions in a web application.
example: An acceptance test fills in a sign-up form and checks that a confirmation appears.

definition: Cardiac stress testing evaluates heart function under exercise or a pharmacological challenge using monitored measurements.
example: A clinician reviews the recorded response to a supervised stress test.

definition: Cardiac valve repair uses clinical interventions to restore function in an existing heart valve without fully replacing it.
example: A heart team evaluates whether a leaking valve can be repaired and explains the options to a patient.

definition: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is an emergency response that uses chest compressions and, where appropriate, ventilation to support circulation during cardiac arrest.
example: A trainee demonstrates resuscitation on a manikin under an instructor’s supervision.

definition: Cardiovascular coding translates documented heart and vascular diagnoses and procedures into standardized healthcare codes.
example: A coder checks that the codes used for a vascular intervention match the clinical record.

definition: Care coordination organizes treatment, communication, and follow-up among patients, caregivers, and service providers.
example: A coordinator confirms that a hospital discharge plan reaches the patient’s primary care practice.

definition: Carrot2 is a software library for clustering collections of text or search results into labeled groups.
example: A search interface groups articles under automatically inferred topics.

definition: CARTO is a geospatial analytics platform for analyzing location data and creating map-based applications.
example: A transport analyst visualizes areas served by existing transit routes.

definition: Cartographic design selects and arranges geographic information and visual symbols so a map communicates clearly.
example: A designer emphasizes public transit lines while de-emphasizing minor streets.

definition: Case analysis examines the facts, context, and alternatives in a specific situation to support an interpretation or decision.
example: A business student compares possible responses to a supplier failure using a detailed written case.

definition: The case method teaches through discussion and analysis of concrete situations rather than exclusively through lectures or abstract exercises.
example: An instructor asks students to defend different decisions as if they were the manager in a case.

definition: CasperJS was a scripting and testing utility for automating browser interactions through PhantomJS or SlimerJS.
example: A maintainer reads a historical browser test that verifies a site’s registration flow.

definition: Casualty movement is the organized relocation or transport of an injured person to safety or appropriate care while accounting for their condition.
example: A first-aid drill evaluates whether participants coordinate a simulated handoff safely.

definition: CatBoost is a gradient boosting library that trains tree ensembles and includes specialized handling of categorical features.
example: An analyst trains a classification model using both transaction amounts and merchant categories.

definition: CCH ProSystem fx Engagement is software for organizing audit and accounting engagement documents, workpapers, and trial balances.
example: An auditor links supporting schedules to a workpaper and routes it for review.

definition: CDC Cyber was a family of large computer systems manufactured by Control Data Corporation.
example: A computing historian investigates how a university scheduled programs on a CDC Cyber system.

definition: cebas finalRender is a rendering engine for producing images from 3D scenes with simulated lighting and materials.
example: A visual effects artist renders a scene to review its reflections and shadows.

definition: Celoxis is project portfolio management software for planning work, tracking delivery, and allocating resources.
example: A manager checks staffing conflicts across several projects.

definition: CentiLeo is a GPU-accelerated renderer for producing images from 3D scenes.
example: A visualization artist renders a scene with complex lighting using a compatible graphics processor.

definition: Cerner refers to a family of healthcare information systems, including electronic health record products.
example: A clinician retrieves documented laboratory results through a hospital’s Cerner system.
sense_note: The name can refer to the vendor or different products, so a specific application may need clarification.

definition: Ceros is a platform for creating and publishing interactive digital content through visual authoring tools.
example: A design team publishes a web report with interactive illustrations and animated sections.

definition: CFWheels is a CFML web framework that structures applications with model-view-controller conventions.
example: A developer adds a controller action and view to display an order record.

definition: Chai.js is a JavaScript assertion library for expressing and checking expected conditions in tests.
example: A unit test checks that a returned record has the required properties and values.

definition: A chain conveyor moves materials or products using one or more driven chains, sometimes with attached carriers.
example: A production line uses a chain conveyor to carry heavy fixtures between workstations.

definition: Chain of custody documents who collected, handled, stored, or transferred an item and when each event occurred.
example: A laboratory records each transfer of a sealed specimen so its integrity can be evaluated.

definition: Chainer was a Python deep-learning framework that constructed computation graphs dynamically during execution.
example: A researcher studies how a legacy Chainer model branches based on input.

definition: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol authenticates a peer through a challenge and a response computed from a shared secret, without transmitting the secret directly.
example: A network administrator recognizes CHAP as the authentication method in a legacy link configuration.

definition: Change agility is the ability of a person or organization to adjust effectively as conditions, priorities, or practices change.
example: A team reallocates work after a supplier delay and tests a new delivery sequence.

definition: Change management planning determines how a transition will be communicated, supported, implemented, and evaluated.
example: A manager prepares training and feedback channels before rolling out a new process.

definition: Changing oil removes used engine or machinery lubricant and replaces it with oil that meets the equipment’s requirements.
example: A mechanic records the oil and filter replacement in a vehicle’s service history.
